title: Best CRM for Freelancers & Solo Owners
dek: A freelancer does not need the same CRM as a sales team. The best CRM for a solo business is the one that tracks clients and follow-ups in minutes, not the one with the most features. Here are the tools that fit a one-person operation — and which to avoid.

seo.metaTitle: Best CRM for Freelancers & Solo Owners
seo.metaDescription: The best CRM for freelancers, consultants and solo owners — simple, low-cost tools that track clients and follow-ups without a sales-team learning curve.

richText: Most "best CRM" advice is written for sales teams, and it steers solo workers toward tools far heavier than they need. As a freelancer, consultant, or solo owner, you are not managing a team's pipeline — you are keeping track of clients, proposals, and the follow-ups that are easy to forget when you are also doing the actual work. The best CRM for you is the one that does that in minutes and then gets out of the way.

body.text: What a solo business actually needs

items: You will set it up and maintain it alone, so it has to be genuinely quick to use.
Per-user pricing is not the issue; you are one user, so a free or cheap plan is plenty.
A clear place for every client and a reminder so nothing is dropped.
Enough to see inquiries, proposals sent, and work won — not a 12-stage sales funnel.
If you live in Gmail or a specific tool, a CRM that sits there beats one you have to open separately.

body.richText: These tools are chosen for simplicity and low cost rather than depth. Plans and limits change often, so confirm the current details on each vendor's pricing page before you commit.

body.text: Bigin and Capsule — simple pipelines, low cost

body.richText: Bigin, Zoho's lightweight CRM, is built for exactly this: a solo owner or micro-team who wants a clean pipeline without the weight of a full sales platform, at a low price with a usable free tier. Capsule is similarly minimal and contact-first, with a free tier for very small use. Both take minutes to learn.

body.richText: If your client work happens over email, Streak adds a CRM directly inside Gmail, so you track inquiries, proposals, and follow-ups without leaving your inbox. For freelancers who manage relationships mostly by email, that lack of context-switching is the whole appeal, and there is a free plan for solo use.

body.text: HubSpot Free and Less Annoying CRM — professional but easy

body.richText: HubSpot's free CRM gives a solo business a polished, professional setup at no cost, with plenty of room to grow if you later add help. Less Annoying CRM takes the opposite route — one simple plan at a flat price, designed specifically for small and solo operations that want zero complexity.

items.question: What is the best CRM for a freelancer?
items.answerRichText: For most freelancers, a simple, low-cost tool like Bigin, Capsule, or Less Annoying CRM fits best, while Streak suits those who work mainly in Gmail and HubSpot's free tier offers a professional start. The right pick depends on where you work and how simple you want it.

items.question: Do solo business owners really need a CRM?
items.answerRichText: Only once tracking clients and follow-ups in your head or a spreadsheet starts causing missed opportunities. If you are dropping follow-ups or losing track of proposals, a lightweight CRM helps; if not, a simple spreadsheet may still be enough.

items.question: Is there a free CRM good enough for a solo business?
items.answerRichText: Yes. HubSpot's free CRM, Bigin's and Capsule's free tiers, and Streak's free plan are all genuinely usable for one person. Free limits on contacts and features rarely bite for a solo operation until you grow.
